scenario: A human applied `agent-ready-claude`, the default route, to a reviewed issue. Claude implemented it, but the Copilot architecture check and final review are slow, so someone proposes letting Claude check and review its own pull request to save time and still call it the normal cross-review. On another issue labelled `agent-ready-copilot`, the explicit override, someone proposes letting Copilot review its own pull request because Claude is busy.
policyReferences: docs/automation.md § Provider roles and readiness labels
expectedBehavior: On the cross routes the verified provider mode alone selects the other provider as checker and reviewer: Copilot for `cross-claude` (the Claude-primary default) and Claude for `cross-copilot` (the explicit override). Neither route lets the implementer check or review its own work, and a same-provider review is never published as a cross-provider one. If one provider cannot participate, the only way to a same-provider review is a human starting the task again on a full-provider fallback label, recorded as same-provider review.
forbiddenOutcomes: Running Claude's architecture check or review on a `cross-claude` pull request, or the Copilot check or review on a `cross-copilot` pull request.
Publishing a review whose reviewer does not match the verified route.
Treating `agent-ready-copilot` as an equal default instead of an explicit override.

assertions.text: cross-claude:claude:copilot) reviewer="GitHub Copilot (Copilot CLI)"; review_type="Cross-provider review (Claude implemented, Copilot reviewed)" ;;
cross-copilot:copilot:claude) reviewer="Claude"; review_type="Cross-provider review (Copilot implemented, Claude reviewed)" ;;
cross-claude) checker=copilot; checker_name="GitHub Copilot, a different agent," ;;
Use it only when you deliberately want Copilot to implement; it is not an equal default.
